purpose: How friends play together: the host's PC runs a DayZ server with the mashup, the launcher opens it to the internet without anyone touching their router, and joiners connect from Melty's join link or an invite code.

rows.doc: maxPlayers written to the generated serverDZ.cfg; also recipe.multiplayer.maxPlayers.
Game port when Melty does not pick one ({port}).
File the launcher writes the host address to.
Fixed words before the address on that log line.
Environment variable that makes Play host a game.
Environment variable carrying Melty's free port.
Environment variable carrying the host address or an invite code.
Invite codes look like RDZ-XXXX-XXXX-XX and encode the host's public address and port.
Most home routers: the launcher opens the port itself and closes it when the host quits.

_unverified.value: Needs a real home router to test.

_unverified.value: Needs a real home router to test.

rows.doc: For hosts whose router refuses automatic port opening. Needs a rendezvous service; not built yet.

Lets clients load the content converted from their own Rivals install (loose files).
Per-player wait between spawn-menu uses on a server.
Steam app id of the free DayZ Server tool the host needs. Steam needs a login that owns DayZ to install it, so the launcher asks Steam to install it once (steam://install/223350).
BI signature version for RivalsDayZ.pbo. The signer is checked byte-for-byte against a known-good v3 signature.

_unverified.value: DayZ servers may hash script files differently from Arma; confirm a hosted server accepts the signed mod (else switch to 2, or sign with DayZ Tools' DSSignFile).
